Title: TypeScript 2.9 Watch API change breaking watch support in ts-loader?

Hey everybody! (and in particular @sheetalkamat and @andy-ms !)

**TypeScript Version:**  2.9.1

Apologies for raising a bug.  I suspect this probably *isn't* a bug.  (Although I suppose it may be.)  I'm raising this issue because it may be a bug; but either way I could really benefit from some guidance. 

I'm one of the maintainers of [ts-loader](https://github.com/TypeStrong/ts-loader).  I was just doing the relevant housekeeping to cut a new release.  I thought I'd switch to building ts-loader with TypeScript 2.9.  However, this presents the following compile error:

```
src/servicesHost.ts:190:9 - error TS2322: Type '{ rootFiles: string[]; options: CompilerOptions; useCaseSensitiveFileNames: () => boolean; getNew...' is not assignable to type 'WatchHost'.
  Types of property 'createProgram' are incompatible.
    Type '{ (newProgram: Program, host: BuilderProgramHost, oldProgram?: BuilderProgram | undefined, config...' is not assignable to type 'CreateProgram<BuilderProgram>'.
      Types of parameters 'newProgram' and 'rootNames' are incompatible.
        Type 'ReadonlyArray<string> | undefined' is not assignable to type 'Program'.
          Type 'undefined' is not assignable to type 'Program'.

190   const watchHost: WatchHost = {
            ~~~~~~~~~
```

The error message isn't as revealing as it might be but I **think** it's related to [`createAbstractBuilder`](https://github.com/Microsoft/TypeScript/blob/master/src/compiler/builder.ts#L570) somehow no longer aligning with [`createProgram`](https://github.com/Microsoft/TypeScript/blob/master/src/compiler/watch.ts#L278).

The easiest way to see this in action is to take the ts-loader source code and amend [this line](https://github.com/TypeStrong/ts-loader/blob/master/src/servicesHost.ts#L242) from: 

```ts
    createProgram: compiler.createAbstractBuilder as any // TODO: Chase up with TypeScript team about API change
```

to:

```ts
    createProgram: compiler.createAbstractBuilder
```

et voila! Compile error.

I've tried digging through the history of [`builder.ts`](https://github.com/Microsoft/TypeScript/commits/master/src/compiler/builder.ts) and I've a hunch that this may be linked to the `strictNullChecks` switch that recently happened.  Unfortunately I'm not getting enough information from the compiler to meaningful progress this.  I'm drawing a blank.

Would you be able to give me some guidance please?   My apologies if I'm missing something super obvious.

Title: TypeScript 2.9 Watch API change breaking watch support in ts-loader?

Hey everybody! (and in particular @sheetalkamat and @andy-ms !)

**TypeScript Version:**  2.9.1

Apologies for raising a bug.  I suspect this probably *isn't* a bug.  (Although I suppose it may be.)  I'm raising this issue because it may be a bug; but either way I could really benefit from some guidance. 

I'm one of the maintainers of [ts-loader](https://github.com/TypeStrong/ts-loader).  I was just doing the relevant housekeeping to cut a new release.  I thought I'd switch to building ts-loader with TypeScript 2.9.  However, this presents the following compile error:

```
src/servicesHost.ts:190:9 - error TS2322: Type '{ rootFiles: string[]; options: CompilerOptions; useCaseSensitiveFileNames: () => boolean; getNew...' is not assignable to type 'WatchHost'.
  Types of property 'createProgram' are incompatible.
    Type '{ (newProgram: Program, host: BuilderProgramHost, oldProgram?: BuilderProgram | undefined, config...' is not assignable to type 'CreateProgram<BuilderProgram>'.
      Types of parameters 'newProgram' and 'rootNames' are incompatible.
        Type 'ReadonlyArray<string> | undefined' is not assignable to type 'Program'.
          Type 'undefined' is not assignable to type 'Program'.

190   const watchHost: WatchHost = {
            ~~~~~~~~~
```

The error message isn't as revealing as it might be but I **think** it's related to [`createAbstractBuilder`](https://github.com/Microsoft/TypeScript/blob/master/src/compiler/builder.ts#L570) somehow no longer aligning with [`createProgram`](https://github.com/Microsoft/TypeScript/blob/master/src/compiler/watch.ts#L278).

The easiest way to see this in action is to take the ts-loader source code and amend [this line](https://github.com/TypeStrong/ts-loader/blob/master/src/servicesHost.ts#L242) from: 

```ts
    createProgram: compiler.createAbstractBuilder as any // TODO: Chase up with TypeScript team about API change
```

to:

```ts
    createProgram: compiler.createAbstractBuilder
```

et voila! Compile error.

I've tried digging through the history of [`builder.ts`](https://github.com/Microsoft/TypeScript/commits/master/src/compiler/builder.ts) and I've a hunch that this may be linked to the `strictNullChecks` switch that recently happened.  Unfortunately I'm not getting enough information from the compiler to meaningful progress this.  I'm drawing a blank.

Would you be able to give me some guidance please?   My apologies if I'm missing something super obvious.

If a file path or function name is available, prefer that concrete name over a broad subsystem label.

Prefer questions about the actual responsibility shown by snippets, not questions that assume the requested feature already exists.

Each check must be answerable from the cited evidence.

If the cited code is contextual, ask what the code establishes in the flow and what next area it points to.

Each check must include concrete expected answer points and a hint that can be hidden behind a click-to-reveal UI.

Do not put understanding-check questions, expected answer points, rubrics, or hints in the visible explanation body. Return all of that only in `understanding_checks`.

## Response format

Return valid JSON only.

`markdown` must be valid Markdown and easy to read in HTML rendering.

`markdown` must not include "Understanding check", "Expected answer points", answer rubrics, or hints.

`understanding_checks` must contain 1 to 3 objects.

Each understanding check must use an id from `question_contexts`.

Each understanding check must cite only evidence refs from its context or the allowed evidence list.

Each understanding check must be answerable from cited snippets. If an answer point is an inference, label it as an inference and include an answer point about the limitation.

Before finalizing, silently check that every concrete code claim has supporting retrieved evidence.

Before finalizing, silently check that requested behavior is not described as existing unless snippets show it.

Before finalizing, silently check that repeated absence caveats are collapsed into the bottom line or final uncertainty section.

{"markdown":"### Bottom line
The issue revolves around a type incompatibility in the TypeScript Watch API, specifically between the `createAbstractBuilder` function in `builder.ts` and the expected `createProgram` signature in the `WatchHost` interface. This mismatch likely stems from changes related to `strictNullChecks` enforcement in TypeScript 2.9, which tightened type definitions and disallowed `undefined` where previously it might have been allowed. Understanding this requires tracing how the watch system constructs programs, how `createProgram` is typed, and how `createAbstractBuilder` fits into this flow.

### System flow
`builder.ts` (where `createAbstractBuilder` is defined) -> `watch.ts` (where `createProgram` and `WatchHost` are defined and used) -> user code (e.g., `servicesHost.ts` in ts-loader) that implements or assigns `createProgram` in a `WatchHost` object.

This flow shows how the builder constructs program instances, how the watch system expects a certain `createProgram` signature, and how user code must conform to that signature.

### Builder (src/compiler/builder.ts)
This file defines `createAbstractBuilder`, a function that creates a builder program for incremental compilation. It returns a `BuilderProgram` instance and accepts parameters including an old program, host, and config file parsing diagnostics. The builder is central to the watch API's incremental compilation.

Understanding `createAbstractBuilder` is crucial because it is assigned to `createProgram` in the watch host, but its signature must match the expected `CreateProgram<BuilderProgram>` type. Changes in strict null checking may have altered the expected parameter types or return types, causing incompatibility.

### Watch API (src/compiler/watch.ts)
This file defines the `WatchHost` interface and the `createProgram` function type expected by the watch system. The `createProgram` function is typed as `CreateProgram<BuilderProgram>`, which expects parameters like `rootNames` (a `ReadonlyArray<string>` or `undefined`) rather than a `Program` instance.

The error message indicates that the `createProgram` function provided (i.e., `createAbstractBuilder`) has incompatible parameter types compared to the expected signature. Specifically, the parameter `newProgram` in `createAbstractBuilder` is a `Program` type, but the watch API expects `rootNames` as a `ReadonlyArray<string> | undefined`. This mismatch is likely due to stricter null checks and type refinements introduced in TypeScript 2.9.

### User code (e.g., src/servicesHost.ts in ts-loader)
In ts-loader's `servicesHost.ts`, the `watchHost` object implements the `WatchHost` interface and assigns `createAbstractBuilder` to its `createProgram` property. Previously, this was cast to `any` to bypass type checking, but removing the cast exposes the type incompatibility.

This shows the practical impact of the API change: user code that previously worked now fails to compile due to stricter type enforcement. To fix this, the user must align the `createProgram` implementation with the new expected signature, possibly by adapting or wrapping `createAbstractBuilder`.

### Implementation / investigation path
To address this issue, start by examining the `createProgram` type definition in the watch API (`watch.ts`) to understand the expected function signature. Then, inspect `createAbstractBuilder` in `builder.ts` to see its parameters and return type. Compare these to identify the mismatch caused by `strictNullChecks` or other type changes.

Next, in user code (e.g., `servicesHost.ts`), adapt the `createProgram` assignment to match the expected signature, potentially by creating a wrapper function that converts parameters appropriately.

### What still needs verification
The retrieved evidence does not include the exact type definitions of `createProgram` or the full signature of `createAbstractBuilder` after the TypeScript 2.9 changes. Verifying these signatures and how `strictNullChecks` affected them would clarify the precise incompatibility.

Further inspection of the watch API's `CreateProgram` type and the builder's `createAbstractBuilder` function in the TypeScript 2.9 source would be the next step.

---

### Summary
The core of the problem is a type mismatch between the watch API's expected `createProgram` function signature and the `createAbstractBuilder` function from the builder module, likely caused by stricter null checking in TypeScript 2.9.
